# Feature Specification: P-RF06 — Semantic search / filter

**Feature Branch**: `006-semantic-search-filter` (spec directory only — no git branch was created automatically; none of this repo's extension hooks are configured)

**Created**: 2026-10-17

**Status**: Draft

**Input**: User description: "P-RF06 — Semantic search / filter over journal entries: Let the user find entries by meaning and narrow them with filters, on the My Records screen, per docs/input/requirements.md section 1 (RF06) and its acceptance criteria; parameter in section 10. Prototype states: the search bar of 'Tela 4 — Meus Registros', 'Tela 4 — Sheet de filtro', and 'Tela 4 — Filtros ativos' (prototype extract, section 2.4, including the note that the backend has no category filter). Backend: GET /entries/search, GET /entries. Test material: docs/input/backend/fixtures/seeded-search-entries.md. Depends on RF07. Do not implement features of later units, extension features (requirements section 2), or change the backend."

## Clarifications

### Session 2026-10-17

- Q: The filter sheet's "TIPO DE ENTRADA" chips allow selecting more than one entry type at once, but both `GET /entries` and `GET /entries/search` accept only a single `source` value per request, and every entry has exactly one `source` — so an entry can never match "every" selected type simultaneously. How should multiple selected entry-type chips be combined, and how should the request(s) be built? → A: Entries having ANY of the selected types are included (OR among the entry-type chips themselves), while that combined set is still ANDed with the active date range and search term. To build it, the app fires one request per selected entry type (each carrying the same `q`/`dateFrom`/`dateTo`), merges the responses, de-duplicates by entry ID, and re-sorts the combined set (by relevance when a search term is active, otherwise reverse-chronological, matching RF07) before rendering — preserving the prototype's multi-select affordance without requiring a backend change. (Resolved by technical judgment per user direction, applying Constitution Principle I.)

# Feature Specification: P-RF04 — Interactive chat with memory (RAG)

**Feature Branch**: `007-chat-memory-rag` (spec directory only — no git branch was created automatically; none of this repo's extension hooks are configured)

**Created**: 2026-10-19

**Status**: Draft

**Input**: User description: "P-RF04 — Interactive chat with memory (RAG): Build the conversation with the AI agent, which answers with context from the user's previous entries, per docs/input/requirements.md section 1 (RF04) and its acceptance criteria. Prototype states: 'Tela 1 — Home/Chat' (default), 'Streaming', 'Falha ao gerar resposta', 'Offline'; 'Tela 3 — Menu lateral' with the session list and the new-conversation action (prototype extract, sections 2.2 and 4). Backend: POST /chat/sessions, GET /chat/sessions, GET /chat/sessions/:id/messages, POST /chat/sessions/:id/messages (SSE), POST /chat/sessions/:id/messages/:userMessageId/retry (requirements, section 6.3). Depends on F000, RF03. Do not implement features of later units, extension features (requirements section 2), or change the backend."

## Clarifications

### Session 2026-10-19

- Q: `POST /chat/sessions` accepts an optional `title`, the backend has no auto-titling logic of its own, and no endpoint exists to rename a session afterward — so whatever the app does at creation time is permanent for that conversation. Should the app send a title derived from the first message, or never send one? → A: The app derives a short title client-side from the first message's text (trimmed, capped to a short preview length) and sends it in `POST /chat/sessions`'s `title` field at the moment that first message creates the session. This is the only mechanism that can ever give a conversation a human-recognizable name, and User Story 4 explicitly requires the side menu to let users find past conversations "by name." (Resolved by technical judgment per user direction, applying Constitution Principle I.)

# Feature Specification: P-RF10 — Save a chat message as an entry

**Feature Branch**: `008-chat-message-bookmark` (spec directory only — no git branch was created automatically; none of this repo's extension hooks are configured)

**Created**: 2026-10-21

**Status**: Draft

**Input**: User description: "P-RF10 — Save a chat message as an entry: Let the user turn one of their own chat messages into a journal entry, per docs/input/requirements.md section 1 (RF10) and its acceptance criteria. Prototype state: 'Tela 1 — Bookmark' with its sub-states (prototype extract, section 2.2). Backend: POST /entries with source `chat` and `chatMessageId` (requirements, section 6.2/6.3). Depends on RF01, RF04. Do not implement features of later units, extension features (requirements section 2), or change the backend."

## User Scenarios & Testing *(mandatory)*

### User Story 1 - Turning a message you just wrote into a journal entry (Priority: P1)

While chatting with the agent, the user says something worth keeping on its own — not through the dedicated capture flow (RF01), but right there in the conversation. They tap a bookmark control on their own message, and it becomes a normal, persisted journal entry without leaving the chat or retyping anything.

A screen whose state depends simultaneously on authentication, synchronization status and entry data.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Session expiration while viewing triggers a new-login prompt without a crash and without losing the scroll position.
- The per-entry synchronization status badge updates independently of the authentication stream.
- No BLoC imports another BLoC directly.

### RF08 — Proactive insights (mechanism)
A suggestion inserted into the chat without the user asking for it. **Scope: only the trigger mechanism, never the quality of the generated text.**

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Trigger after N = 5 user messages OR T = 2 min of inactivity — fires exactly once per satisfied condition.
- If insight generation fails (timeout / network error), the main chat keeps working normally.
- Dismissing the insight does not change the scroll position or the state of the main conversation.

### RF09 — Temporal summaries / dashboard
An evolution chart with a textual summary, computed on demand when the Settings tab is opened. **Scope: aggregation and rendering, never the quality of the narrative text.**

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Renders correctly in three scenarios: zero entries, one entry, more than 30 entries.
- The aggregation recalculates correctly after an entry is created (cache-invalidation test). Entries are immutable: there is no `PATCH /entries/:id` or `DELETE /entries/:id` in the backend, and no screen describes an edit or delete action on an entry.
- The AI narrative text is checked only for not breaking the UI in extreme cases — never for its content.

### RF10 — Save a chat message as an entry
A button on each user message in the chat that converts it into a persisted entry — for moments when the user states relevant information during the conversation, not only through dedicated capture (RF01). It reuses the same `POST /entries` pipeline (PII check + embedding), with the origin marked as `chat`.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- The chat feature triggers the creation of the entry through a shared interface / use case, never by directly importing a repository or data source of the entries feature — a violation here also breaks RNF06.
- Saving the same message twice does not create duplicate entries (idempotency).
- A failure to save (network unavailable) keeps the conversation working normally, and the button returns to a state that allows trying again — the same failure-isolation pattern as RF08.
- Only user messages have the button — AI responses cannot become entries.

---

## 2. Extension features — not implemented

They keep the "essence" of the original product flow and exist in the prototype, but **receive no functional implementation**. A menu entry may exist as a placeholder.

## 9. Technology stack

| Layer | Choice |
|---|---|
| Mobile app | Flutter, BLoC, Clean Architecture |
| Backend | Already built and frozen; consumed through its API |
| Infrastructure | Supabase (Postgres + pgvector + Storage + Auth + RLS) |
| Chat / vision / OCR / summary / insights / dashboard / PII | Claude Sonnet 5 (chat) + Claude Haiku 4.5 (the rest) — in the backend |
| Embeddings (RAG) | Voyage AI `voyage-4` — in the backend |
| Speech-to-text (audio transcription) | Whisper on-device (`whisper_ggml`); audio never reaches the backend |
| Error handling | `fpdart` (`Either<Failure, T>`) |
| Layer rule | RNF06 |
| Test coverage | RNF07 |

---

## 10. Configuration parameters

Fixed values — not to be reinterpreted.

| Parameter | Value | Requirement |
|---|---|---|
| Background session timeout | 5 min | RF03 |
| Search debounce | 300 ms | RF06 |
| Proactive insight trigger | 5 messages OR 2 min of inactivity | RF08 |
| Dashboard rendering scenarios | 0 / 1 / > 30 entries | RF09 |
| Minimum test coverage (domain) | ≥ 80% | RNF07 |
| Local UI latency | < 100 ms | RNF01 |
| Loading-indicator threshold | > 300 ms | RNF01 |
| Network-error scenarios tested | 5 endpoints × 3 failures = 15 | RNF09 |

---

## 11. Error codes (RNF09)

Every endpoint returns `{ code, message, retryable }`. Minimum codes the app handles:

| Code | Situation | `retryable` |
|---|---|---|
| `AUTH_EXPIRED` | Session expired, re-authentication needed | no |
| `AUTH_INVALID` | Invalid credentials / biometrics | no |
| `NETWORK_TIMEOUT` | Request exceeded the time limit | yes |
| `NETWORK_OFFLINE` | No connection — action blocked (see RF04/RF06) | yes |
| `VALIDATION_ERROR` | Malformed request body | no |
| `PII_CHECK_FAILED` | PII check failed before persisting | yes |
| `EMBEDDING_FAILED` | Voyage AI unavailable / error | yes |
| `AI_GENERATION_TIMEOUT` | Claude did not respond in time (chat/insight/summary/dashboard) | yes |
| `NOT_FOUND` | Resource does not exist or does not belong to the user | no |
| `RATE_LIMITED` | Request limit exceeded | yes |

The complete, closed list of the backend's 13 codes, with HTTP statuses, is in `docs/input/backend/error-taxonomy.md`.

---

## 12. Delivery order

Work is delivered in units, one per functional requirement, preceded by a foundation unit, in this order:

**F000 → RF03 → RF01 → RF02 → RF07 → RF06 → RF04 → RF10 → RF08 → RF05 → RF09**

- **F000 (foundation)** covers what no single requirement owns but all of them use: project scaffold, `design_tokens.dart`, HTTP client returning `Either`, login and sign-up (Screen 0.1a in the prototype), base navigation and expired-session handling.
- RF10 comes after RF01 and RF04; RF08 comes after RF04.

---

## 13. Technical constraints

## 3. Quality requirements

| ID | Requirement | Target |
|---|---|---|
| RNF06 | Zero layer violations — the domain layer does not import `package:flutter` nor classes from `data/` | 0 violations |
| RNF07 | Minimum test coverage of the domain layer (`lib/**/domain/**`) | ≥ 80% |
| RNF08 | Visual fidelity to the prototype — the primary color matches the prototype's hex value, typography matches family and size, spacing matches the prototype; no visual value hardcoded outside the central file `design_tokens.dart` | Every screen faithful in color, typography and spacing; 0 hardcoded values |
| RNF09 | Consistent network-error handling — `Either<Failure, T>` pattern via `fpdart` in every repository; every write endpoint (5 endpoints) handles three failure types — timeout, malformed response, no connection — covered by tests with `mocktail` | 0 repository signatures outside the pattern; 15 of 15 scenarios handled |

## 4. Other non-functional requirements

RNF01 — Interaction latency (a local action is reflected in the UI in < 100 ms; any network call above 300 ms shows a loading indicator) · RNF02 — PII stripping (via Claude Haiku 4.5 with a structured prompt / tool use, not a dedicated NER model) · RNF03 — Zero data retention · RNF04 — RLS (Row Level Security) · RNF05 — Hard delete of account and data (LGPD).

**Known limitation:** the system has no protocol for detecting or responding to risk signals (suicidal ideation, self-harm) in entries or chat messages. Since the product is not framed as a mental-health app, this absence is an explicit scope decision.

---

## 5. Interface architecture and screen flow

### 5.1 Visual foundation (design system)
Minimalist identity, a warm and neutral palette, readable sans-serif typography, standardized components (buttons, chat bubbles, cards). This foundation is the direct object of RNF08. Tokens: `docs/input/prototype/prototype-extract.md`.

### 5.2 Screens

**Screen 0 — Splash:** initial loading; checks the connection and syncs the cache in the background. *Connects to: RF06, RNF01.*

**Screen 0.1 — Authentication vault:** biometric/PIN barrier before access. *Connects to: RF03.*

**Screen 1 — Home (chat):** main screen, continuous conversation, "+" button for multimodal input, AI status indicator, "save to journal" button on each user message. *Connects to: RF04, RF08, RF10, RNF01, RNF09.*

**Screen 2 — Insertion Modal:** overlay with three ways to capture — raw text field, microphone (audio) and gallery/camera (photo) — with a transcription indicator. Every capture here creates a persisted entry, never a chat message. *Connects to: RF01, RF02.*

**Screen 3 — Side menu (sidebar):** navigation hub, session history, access to My Records / Action Plans / Settings, and a "Novo Chat" button that opens Screen 1 in its empty state. *Connects to: RF04 (via the "Novo Chat" button); the other items are pure navigation.*

**Screen 4 — My Records:** consolidated timeline, filters, manual tags (extension, section 2), export. *Connects to: RF07, RF06, RF05.*

**Screen 5 — Action Plans:** simple Kanban board (columns "A Fazer" / "Em Andamento" / "Concluído") with static example cards. *(Extension — section 2.)*

**Screen 6 — Settings and profile:** evolution dashboard, persona selector — "Analítico" / "Empático" / "Socrático" (extension, section 2; it would only change the system-prompt string of RF04), delete account. *Connects to: RF09, RNF05.*

---

## 6. Backend endpoint inventory

The backend is already built and frozen. The API contract, `docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml`, is the source of truth; this section is a reading of it oriented by screen and requirement. How to build the real URL of each operation: `docs/input/backend/README.md`.

Every endpoint returns errors in the standard contract of RNF09 — `{ code, message, retryable }` — and is protected by RLS in Supabase. AI providers: Claude (chat, vision/OCR, summary, insights, dashboard, PII detection) and Voyage AI (embeddings) — the backend's only two external AI dependencies. Audio transcription (speech-to-text) runs on-device (Whisper) and never reaches the backend as an audio file.

### 6.1 Authentication and session
| Endpoint | Requirement | AI involved |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /auth/signup` | RF03 | — |
| `POST /auth/login` | RF03 | — |
| `POST /auth/refresh` | RF03, RF07 | — |
| `GET /auth/session` | RF07 | — |
| `POST /auth/logout` | RF03 | — |

**No "biometric-unlock" endpoint — intentional:** the Face ID / Touch ID / PIN barrier of Screen 0.1 is validated entirely on the device, never on the server. The backend only stores the preference (`biometricEnabled`, read and written via `PATCH /account/settings`, section 6.7) — it validates no biometrics. After passing the local barrier, the app uses the existing session (renewed via `POST /auth/refresh` when needed, or `POST /auth/login` if it has fully expired).

### 6.2 Ingestion and entries
| Endpoint | Requirement | AI involved |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /media/ocr` — the image is not persisted; only the extracted text moves on | RF02 | Claude Haiku 4.5 (vision) |
| `POST /entries` — creates an entry; internally triggers the PII check and embedding generation; accepts `source` (`manual`/`audio`/`photo`/`chat`) and `chatMessageId` when the origin is the chat | RF01, RF02, RF10 | Claude Haiku 4.5 (PII) + Voyage AI (embedding) |
| `GET /entries` — filters by `source`/`dateFrom`/`dateTo`; tags appear only embedded in the response, read-only | RF07 | — |
| `GET /entries/:id` | RF07 | — |

**No entry editing or deletion, and no tag endpoint — intentional:** entries are immutable once created ("original content intact, never censored"); there is no `PATCH`/`DELETE /entries/:id`. Tags are populated only by test seed data — no endpoint creates, deletes or filters by tag or category (see RF06). This is consistent with section 2: dynamic categorization was simplified to manual tags that receive no functional implementation.

### 6.3 Chat and memory (RAG)
| Endpoint | Requirement | AI involved |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /chat/sessions` — blocked offline | RF04 | — |
| `GET /chat/sessions` — works offline (cache) | RF04, RF07 | — |
| `GET /chat/sessions/:id/messages` — works offline (cache) | RF04 | — |
| `POST /chat/sessions/:id/messages` — streaming (SSE); blocked offline | RF04 | Voyage AI (question embedding) + Claude Sonnet 5 (response) |
| `POST /chat/sessions/:id/messages/:userMessageId/retry` — regenerates the response without duplicating the user's question; it supports "partial message visible with a failure indication, and a way to try again" in RF04 | RF04 | Voyage AI (embedding, reused from cache) + Claude Sonnet 5 (response) |
| `POST /chat/sessions/:id/insight` | RF08 | Claude Haiku 4.5 |
| `POST /entries` — called from the "save to journal" button (see 6.2) | RF10 | Claude Haiku 4.5 (PII) + Voyage AI (embedding) |

### 6.4 Search
| Endpoint | Requirement | AI involved |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /entries/search?q=&source=&dateFrom=&dateTo=&limit=` — no `category` (see RF06) | RF06 | Voyage AI (query embedding) |

### 6.5 Export
| Endpoint | Requirement | AI involved |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /export/summary` — asynchronous job | RF05 | Claude Haiku 4.5 |
| `GET /export/:jobId/status` | RF05 | — |
| `GET /export/:jobId/download` | RF05 | — |

### 6.6 Dashboard
| Endpoint | Requirement | AI involved |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /dashboard/aggregate?period=` — separate from the text so it does not block the chart | RF09 | — |
| `GET /dashboard/narrative?period=` | RF09 | Claude Haiku 4.5 |

### 6.7 Account
| Endpoint | Requirement | AI involved |
|---|---|---|
| `PATCH /account/settings` — includes the persona toggle (extension) | RNF05, extension | — |
| `DELETE /account` | RNF05 | — |

## 2. Navigable states

Names as they appear in the prototype. The prototype's own state catalog has 32 entries: Tela 0 — Splash; Tela 0.1 — Biometria; Tela 0.1a — Entrar / criar conta; Tela 0.1b — PIN inicial; Tela 0.1c — PIN após falha; Tela 1 — Home / Chat; Tela 2 — Texto, Áudio (Gravando, Processando, Transcrito, Erro), Foto (Captura, Processando OCR, Reconhecido, Erro); Tela 3 — Menu lateral; Tela 1 — Sessão expirada; Tela 4 — Meus Registros, Estado vazio, Sheet de filtro, Filtros ativos; Exportar — Pendente, Processando, Concluído, Erro, Período vazio; Tela 5 — Planos de Ação **[ext]**; Tela 6 — Configurações, Dashboard zero entradas, Dashboard uma entrada, Narrativa indisponível, Confirmar exclusão. The tables below group them by screen; some rows describe variations inside one state (e.g., the bookmark sub-states, the streaming response). Extension states (requirements, section 2) are marked **[ext]**.

### 2.1 Entry and authentication
| State | What it shows |
|---|---|
| Tela 0 — Splash | Wordmark "Cerne" centered on dark green, 3 loading dots; lasts 1.8 s and moves on automatically. |
| Tela 0.1 — Biometria | Fingerprint circle, title "Toque para desbloquear", link "Usar PIN", secondary link "usar e-mail e senha" near the bottom. |
| Tela 0.1a — Entrar | Login mode: title "Bem-vindo de volta", fields E-mail and Senha, CTA "Entrar", toggle link, link "usar biometria". |
| Tela 0.1a — Criar conta | Same screen in sign-up mode: title "Crie sua conta", CTA "Criar conta" (toggled by a text link, not a separate screen). |
| Tela 0.1b — PIN inicial | Title "Digite seu PIN", 4 progress dots, 3×4 numeric keypad with backspace; after the 4th digit, moves on after 350 ms. |
| Tela 0.1c — PIN após falha | Same as 0.1b plus the error band "Não foi possível reconhecer — digite seu PIN". |

### 2.2 Conversation
| State | What it shows |
|---|---|
| Tela 1 — Home/Chat (default) | Messages going back and forth; dark green fixed header with ☰ and wordmark; composer with "+", placeholder "Escreva uma mensagem...", send icon. |
| Tela 1 — Streaming | AI response revealed progressively with a pulsing cursor. |
| Tela 1 — Insight | Insight card with ochre spine, label "INSIGHT", "x" to dismiss, interleaved in the messages. |
| Tela 1 — Falha ao gerar resposta | Incomplete AI message with "Falha ao gerar resposta — toque para tentar novamente" in red, in place of the time. |
| Tela 1 — Bookmark | Bookmark on each user message with 4 sub-states: `idle`, `saving` (spinner), `saved` (ochre check), `error` (red warning). |
| Tela 1 — Offline | Blue-gray banner "Sem conexão — histórico disponível, novas mensagens bloqueadas"; send icon disabled. |
| Tela 1 — Sessão expirada | Light scrim over the chat (still readable), centered card with lock icon, title "Sessão expirada", text saying history and scroll position are kept, button "Entrar novamente". |
| Tela 3 — Menu lateral | Drawer: initials avatar and name; section "CONVERSAS" with past sessions (title + timestamp); items "Meus Registros", "Planos de Ação", "Configurações"; new-conversation action. |

### 2.3 Insertion modal (bottom sheet over Home/Chat; 9 states)
Common structure: "x" to close and a 3-tab bar (Texto / Áudio / Foto); the active tab has a filled dark-green background.

| State | What it shows |
|---|---|
| Texto | Multiline field, placeholder "Escreva livremente...", button "Salvar". |
| Áudio — Gravando | Red stop button, animated 12-bar waveform, monospace timer (e.g., "00:12"). |
| Áudio — Processando | Spinner in place of stop; frozen, faded waveform (opacity .35); text "Transcrevendo..."; label "00:42 de áudio". |
| Áudio — Transcrito | Editable transcribed text; original audio duration in mono; "Salvar" enabled. |
| Áudio — Erro | Red warning icon, "Não foi possível transcrever", outline button "Tentar novamente". |
| Foto — Captura | Two large buttons, "Câmera" and "Galeria". |
| Foto — Processando OCR | Photo thumbnail, spinner, "Reconhecendo texto...". |
| Foto — Reconhecido | Small thumbnail next to the extracted (editable) text; "Salvar". |
| Foto — Erro | Thumbnail kept, warning icon, "Não foi possível reconhecer o texto", button "Tentar novamente" and secondary text action "Salvar só a foto". |

### 2.4 Records
| State | What it shows |
|---|---|
| Tela 4 — Meus Registros (default) | Records grouped by date ("Hoje", "Ontem", dates); each card with a spine colored by origin, source icon, time, sync indicator (green "sincronizado" / ochre "sincronizando" / red "erro de sync"), text excerpt, category chips when present; header with back arrow, title, download icon; search bar "Buscar nos registros..." with a funnel button. |
| Tela 4 — Vazio | Large notebook icon, "Nenhum registro ainda", CTA "Criar primeiro registro". |
| Tela 4 — Filtros ativos | Removable chips under the search bar with the applied filters, link "Limpar filtros"; funnel button filled. |
| Tela 4 — Sheet de filtro | Groups "INTERVALO DE DATA" (Todo o período / Esta semana / Este mês, single choice), "CATEGORIA" (chips: trabalho, rotina, descanso, relações), "TIPO DE ENTRADA" (chips: manual, áudio, foto, chat); "Aplicar" and "Limpar". **Note:** the backend has no category filter (requirements, RF06); categories are the tags extension. |

### 2.5 Export (bottom sheet over Tela 4; 5 states)
| State | What it shows |
|---|---|
| Pendente | Spinner, "Preparando exportação...". |
| Processando | "Gerando resumo com IA...", progress bar. |
| Concluído | Green check, "Resumo pronto", buttons "Baixar PDF" (primary) and "Baixar dados brutos" (outline). |

1	# Feature Specification: P-RF04 — Interactive chat with memory (RAG)
2	
3	**Feature Branch**: `007-chat-memory-rag` (spec directory only — no git branch was created automatically; none of this repo's extension hooks are configured)
4	
5	**Created**: 2026-10-19
6	
7	**Status**: Draft
8	
9	**Input**: User description: "P-RF04 — Interactive chat with memory (RAG): Build the conversation with the AI agent, which answers with context from the user's previous entries, per docs/input/requirements.md section 1 (RF04) and its acceptance criteria. Prototype states: 'Tela 1 — Home/Chat' (default), 'Streaming', 'Falha ao gerar resposta', 'Offline'; 'Tela 3 — Menu lateral' with the session list and the new-conversation action (prototype extract, sections 2.2 and 4). Backend: POST /chat/sessions, GET /chat/sessions, GET /chat/sessions/:id/messages, POST /chat/sessions/:id/messages (SSE), POST /chat/sessions/:id/messages/:userMessageId/retry (requirements, section 6.3). Depends on F000, RF03. Do not implement features of later units, extension features (requirements section 2), or change the backend."
10	
11	## Clarifications
12	
13	### Session 2026-10-19
14	
15	- Q: `POST /chat/sessions` accepts an optional `title`, the backend has no auto-titling logic of its own, and no endpoint exists to rename a session afterward — so whatever the app does at creation time is permanent for that conversation. (Resolved by technical judgment per user direction, applying Constitution Principle I.)
16	- Q: `GET /chat/sessions` is cursor-paginated (`cursor`/`limit`, default 20, max 50) and its items carry no documented sort order; the prototype's side-menu extract shows a flat "CONVERSAS" list with no load-more control. (Resolved by technical judgment per user direction, applying Constitution Principle I.)
18	
19	## User Scenarios & Testing *(mandatory)*
20	
21	### User Story 1 - Getting an answer grounded in your own journal (Priority: P1)
22	
23	A user opens the chat and asks the AI agent something related to their life, without repeating what they already wrote elsewhere. The agent's answer reflects relevant things the user recorded before, not just the current message in isolation, and the exchange stays on screen as a normal, persisted conversation the user can come back to.
24	
25	**Why this priority**: This is the entire premise of RF04 — "memory" via semantic search over past entries. Without it, the screen is just a generic chat window with no connection to the rest of the product.
26	
27	**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by seeding an account with a prior entry about a specific topic, sending a chat message that references that topic without quoting it verbatim, and confirming the agent's response demonstrates awareness of the seeded entry's content.
28	
29	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
30	
31	1. **Given** the user has at least one prior entry about a specific topic, **When** they send a chat message related to that topic, **Then** the agent's response reflects information from that entry, even though the message itself never restated it.
32	2. **Given** a conversation already has one or more exchanges, **When** the user leaves the screen and returns later (including after an app restart), **Then** the full exchange history is still present, in the same order, without needing to be resent.
33	3. **Given** the user sends a chat message, **When** the message is accepted, **Then** it is stored and displayed as part of the conversation but does **not** create a journal entry — chat messages are conversational only, with no automatic persistence as an entry (the one exception, an explicit save action, belongs to a later unit and is out of scope here).
34	
35	---
36	
37	### User Story 2 - Always knowing what the agent is doing (Priority: P1)
38	
39	While waiting for or reading a response, the user can always tell, at a glance, which of three things is happening: the answer is still arriving, it finished successfully, or it failed — and a response that stops arriving partway through never just vanishes.
40	
41	**Why this priority**: RF04's acceptance criteria explicitly require these three states and the no-disappearing-partial-message rule; without a clear, honest status, users cannot trust the chat enough to rely on it.
42	
43	**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by sending a message and observing the UI progress through the "processing/streaming" state into either "complete response" or "error," and separately by forcing a connection drop mid-response and confirming the partial text stays visible with a failure indication instead of disappearing.
44	
45	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
46	
47	1. **Given** the user has just sent a message, **When** the agent begins producing a reply, **Then** the response is revealed progressively (streaming) with a visible in-progress indicator, distinct from a finished message.
48	2. **Given** a response finishes streaming normally, **When** the last token arrives, **Then** the message is shown in its final, complete form with its timestamp, no longer carrying any in-progress indicator.
49	3. **Given** the connection drops, or the backend returns an error, while a response is still arriving, **When** that happens, **Then** whatever text had already arrived stays visible, together with a clear failure indication in place of the timestamp — the message is never removed or left in an ambiguous unfinished-looking state.
50	
51	---
52	
53	### User Story 3 - Recovering from a failed response without losing the conversation (Priority: P2)
54	
55	A response fails or is cut short. The user taps the failed message and gets a fresh attempt at an answer to the same question, without having to retype it, without creating a duplicate question in the history, and without disturbing the rest of the conversation.
56	
57	**Why this priority**: A direct extension of Story 2's failure state — the failure indication is only useful if there's a documented way out of it, and the requirement calls this out explicitly ("a way to try again" is part of RF04's own scope).
58	
59	**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by forcing a response failure, tapping the failed message to retry, and confirming a new response is generated for the same original question, with the user's question appearing exactly once in the history.
60	
61	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
62	
63	1. **Given** a message shows the "Falha ao gerar resposta" state, **When** the user taps it, **Then** a new response attempt starts for that same original question, going through the same processing/streaming → complete/error states as a normal response.
64	2. **Given** a retry is in progress or has completed, **When** the history is inspected, **Then** the user's original question appears exactly once — retrying never duplicates the question, only replaces the failed answer with a new attempt.
65	3. **Given** the retry itself fails again, **When** that happens, **Then** the message returns to the same failure state with the same way to try again — retrying is not limited to a single attempt.
66	
67	---
68	
69	### User Story 4 - Organizing conversations from the side menu (Priority: P2)
70	
71	A user wants to start a brand-new conversation without losing an existing one, and wants to see and return to past conversations by name and recency from the side menu.
72	
73	**Why this priority**: RF04's own scope explicitly includes the side menu's session list and "Novo Chat" action (prototype extract, sections 2.2 and 4) — without it, a user has no way to manage more than one conversation at a time.
74	
75	**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by having at least one existing conversation, opening the side menu, confirming it lists past sessions with a title and timestamp, tapping "Novo Chat," confirming the chat screen shows an empty conversation, and confirming the prior conversation is unchanged when reopened from the list.
76	
77	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
78	
79	1. **Given** the user has one or more existing conversations, **When** they open the side menu, **Then** a "CONVERSAS" section lists each one with a title and a timestamp.
80	2. **Given** the side menu is open, **When** the user taps the new-conversation action ("Novo Chat"), **Then** the chat screen shows an empty conversation, ready to accept a first message, without discarding any previous conversation.
81	3. **Given** the user selects a past conversation from the list, **When** it opens, **Then** its full message history is shown exactly as it was left.
82	
83	---
84	
85	### User Story 5 - Reading history while offline (Priority: P3)
86	
87	A user without a connection can still read everything they already loaded, but cannot send anything new, and is told clearly why.
88	
89	**Why this priority**: Explicitly one of the four required prototype states for this screen, and it protects against the worse failure mode of a chat screen that looks broken or loses content when connectivity drops — but it is a secondary concern relative to the core conversation and failure-recovery loops above.
90	
91	**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by loading a conversation, simulating a loss of connectivity, confirming the existing history stays visible and scrollable, confirming the send control is disabled with an explanatory banner, and confirming sending is not possible until connectivity returns.
92	
93	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
94	
95	1. **Given** a conversation is already loaded, **When** the device goes offline, **Then** the existing message history remains visible and scrollable, and a banner explains that new messages are blocked.
96	2. **Given** the device is offline, **When** the user looks at the composer, **Then** the send control is visibly disabled — no message can be sent until the connection returns.
97	3. **Given** the connection returns, **When** the user resumes using the screen, **Then** the send control re-enables and new messages can be sent normally.
98	4. **Given** the user has previously opened more than one conversation while online, **When** the device goes offline and the user switches between those previously-opened conversations from the side menu, **Then** each one's cached history is shown exactly as it was left, not just the conversation open at the moment connectivity dropped.
99	
100	---
101	
102	### Edge Cases
103	
104	- The user tries to send an empty or whitespace-only message: the send control stays disabled/inactive, and no request is made.
105	- A message at or near the backend's maximum length is sent: the system either prevents exceeding that maximum before sending or surfaces the backend's resulting validation error clearly, without losing the text the user typed.
106	- A message is sent while a previous response in the same conversation is still streaming, or is sitting in the failed/"tap to retry" state: the composer stays disabled until that turn resolves (completes or is retried to a new resolution), so a session never has two responses racing at once.
107	- The session expires (RF03/RF07's existing "Sessão expirada" behavior) while a response is mid-stream or while viewing history: the existing overlay is shown, history and scroll position are preserved underneath it, and once the user re-authenticates, the conversation resumes exactly where it was — this unit reuses that behavior rather than redefining it.
108	- The user navigates away from a conversation (e.g., via the side menu) while a response is still streaming: when the user returns to that conversation, the message reflects whatever the backend ultimately recorded for it (complete or failed) rather than being stuck in a stale in-progress state tied to a connection that no longer exists.
109	- An account has zero conversations yet (first-ever use of chat): the chat screen still shows a ready-to-use empty conversation, and a session is created at the point the first message is actually sent.
110	- The user retries a failed message that is not the most recent message in the conversation: the retry still succeeds and only affects that specific message's response, leaving every later message in the conversation untouched.
111	- An account has more conversations than fit in one backend page of `GET /chat/sessions` (more than its default/max `limit`): scrolling to the bottom of the side menu's "CONVERSAS" section fetches the next page via `cursor` rather than silently stopping at the first page.
112	- The user is offline and selects, from the side menu, a conversation that was never opened while online: no cached data exists for it, so the screen shows the standard no-connection state instead of any content, distinct from the normal offline case of browsing an already-cached conversation.
113	- Opening the side menu's conversation list, the export job, dashboard, filters, action-plan board, and every other screen or action not named in this feature's scope: unaffected by this unit and not touched by it.
114	
115	## Requirements *(mandatory)*
116	
117	### Functional Requirements
118	
119	- **FR-001**: The system MUST let an authenticated user send a text message in an active conversation (`POST /chat/sessions/:id/messages`) and receive a response generated with the help of the user's own previously captured entries — the response MUST be able to reflect information from a prior entry that the user's message does not itself restate.
120	- **FR-002**: Every message the user sends and every response the agent produces MUST be persisted as part of the conversation (`chat_messages`) and MUST still be present, in the same order, the next time that conversation is opened — including after the app is closed and reopened (`GET /chat/sessions/:id/messages`).
121	- **FR-003**: Sending a chat message MUST NOT create a journal entry under any circumstance handled by this unit; the only path from a chat message to a persisted entry is the explicit save action of a later unit (RF10), which this unit does not implement.
122	- **FR-004**: While a response is being generated, the system MUST render it in a visibly distinct "processing/streaming" state (content revealed progressively, in-progress indicator) and MUST transition it to one of exactly two end states: "complete response" (final text, timestamp shown, no in-progress indicator) or an error state ("Falha ao gerar resposta," shown in place of the timestamp). A response MUST always end in one of these three states — streaming, complete, or error — never left ambiguous.
123	- **FR-005**: If the response stream is interrupted before completion (connection drop, backend error, or any other cause), the system MUST keep whatever partial text had already arrived visible, together with the failure indication — it MUST NOT remove, hide, or blank out a partial message.
124	- **FR-006**: A message in the error state MUST be tappable to trigger a retry (`POST /chat/sessions/:id/messages/:userMessageId/retry`) that regenerates the response to that same original question. A retry MUST NOT duplicate the user's original question in the conversation, and MUST go through the same processing/streaming → complete/error states as any other response. Retrying MUST remain available after a retry itself fails, with no fixed limit on the number of attempts, and MUST remain available on any message in the error state regardless of how much later conversation exists after it.
125	- **FR-007**: While a response in the current conversation is streaming or sitting in the error state awaiting retry, the system MUST keep the message-send control disabled, re-enabling it only once that response reaches a final state (complete, or retried to a new resolution) — so a single conversation never has two responses in flight at once.
126	- **FR-008**: The side menu MUST show a "CONVERSAS" section listing the user's existing conversations (`GET /chat/sessions`), each with its title and a timestamp, ordered by most recent activity (latest `lastUserMessageAt` first). If the account has more sessions than fit in one backend page, the list MUST fetch further pages via the endpoint's `cursor` as the user scrolls to the bottom of the section, so every conversation stays reachable.
127	- **FR-009**: The side menu MUST offer a "Novo Chat" action that opens the chat screen in an empty conversation state, ready to accept a first message, without discarding or altering any existing conversation. Selecting an existing conversation from the list MUST open it with its full message history intact, exactly as it was left.
128	- **FR-010**: A new conversation (`POST /chat/sessions`) MUST only be created at the point a first message is actually sent into an empty conversation state — opening an empty conversation state (via "Novo Chat," or on an account with no conversations yet) MUST NOT by itself create a session with no messages in it. That creation call MUST include a `title` derived from the first message's own text (a short, trimmed preview), so the new conversation has a distinguishable, human-recognizable name in the side menu from the moment it exists — the backend has no auto-titling of its own and no later rename endpoint.
129	- **FR-011**: While the device is offline, the system MUST keep every previously-opened conversation's history, and the side menu's own "CONVERSAS" list, visible, scrollable, and switchable from the local cache — not only the one conversation that happened to be open when connectivity dropped — MUST disable the send control, and MUST show an explanatory message that new messages are blocked until the connection returns. Selecting a conversation that was never opened while online, while currently offline, MUST show the standard no-connection state rather than any content, since nothing was ever cached for it. Sending MUST become possible again as soon as connectivity is restored, with no manual reset required.
130	- **FR-012**: The system MUST NOT attempt to create a new conversation or send/retry a message while offline — both actions require a connection and MUST be blocked client-side rather than attempted and failed.
131	- **FR-013**: The screen MUST reuse the existing session-expiration handling (RF03/RF07's "Sessão expirada" overlay: history and scroll position preserved, re-authentication returning to the same conversation state) rather than introducing a separate expiration treatment for chat.
132	- **FR-014**: This unit MUST NOT implement the "save message as entry" button (RF10), the proactive-insight card (RF08), AI-persona selection as an active setting (extension, requirements section 2 — persona is only read at session creation as whatever the backend already returns), or any change to the backend, its API contract, or its configuration.
133	
134	### Key Entities
135	
136	- **Chat Session**: One conversation thread, identified by an id, with a title derived client-side from its first message at creation time and shown in the side menu's "CONVERSAS" section (a defensive generic placeholder is shown only if a session is ever encountered with an empty title), the persona that was in effect when it was created (read-only here — not user-editable in this unit), and timestamps including when it was created and when it last received a user message (the latter drives the side menu's ordering).
137	- **Chat Message**: One turn inside a Chat Session — either the user's question or the agent's response — with its content, its position in the conversation, and its status (still arriving, complete, or failed). A failed message is the one eligible for retry; retrying produces a new resolution for the same original question rather than a new message pair.
138	- **Context used for a response**: The set of the user's own prior entries the agent draws on to ground a given response. It is retrieved automatically for every response and is not displayed to the user as a separate citation list — the prototype defines no such element — but it is what makes a response "grounded" rather than generic, per User Story 1.
139	
140	## Success Criteria *(mandatory)*
141	
142	### Measurable Outcomes
143	
144	- **SC-001**: When a seeded prior entry exists on a topic, a chat message about that topic that does not restate the entry's content still produces a response reflecting that entry's information, in 100% of tested cases.
145	- **SC-002**: Every sent or retried message ends in exactly one of the three defined states (streaming → complete, or streaming → error) with zero cases observed stuck in an undefined or ambiguous state.
146	- **SC-003**: In 100% of forced stream-interruption scenarios, the partial response text remains visible on screen together with its failure indication — never disappearing.
147	- **SC-004**: Across repeated retries of the same failed message, the user's original question appears exactly once in the conversation history, with zero observed duplicates.
148	- **SC-005**: Conversation history is preserved exactly (same messages, same order) across an app restart and across switching away from and back to a conversation via the side menu, in 100% of tested cases.
149	- **SC-006**: While offline, 100% of the history of every previously-opened conversation stays readable and switchable from the side menu (not only the one open at disconnect), and the send control is visibly disabled for the entire duration of the outage, re-enabling within one interaction of connectivity returning.
150	- **SC-007**: On an account with more conversations than one backend page of `GET /chat/sessions` returns, 100% of them remain reachable from the side menu by scrolling, with zero conversations permanently hidden.
151	
152	## Assumptions
153	
154	- A conversation ("session") is created lazily, only when the user actually sends a first message into an empty conversation state, rather than eagerly when "Novo Chat" is tapped or when the chat screen is simply opened — this keeps the backend free of empty sessions and matches `POST /chat/sessions` accepting no required `title`. Re-opening the app resumes whichever conversation the user was last in (if any exist); when none exist yet, the screen shows the same empty, ready-to-send state "Novo Chat" also produces.
155	- The "context" step of the backend's streaming sequence (`message_created -> context -> token* -> done|error`) is an internal signal the client may use to drive its own progress indicator, not a citation list rendered to the user — the prototype defines no UI for displaying which entries were used.
156	- A session's `personaSnapshot` (requirements section 2's persona extension) is read and stored as whatever the backend returns at session creation; this unit does not add any UI for choosing or changing it.
157	- Network-error handling for this screen's write calls (send, retry, create session) follows the same retryable/non-retryable pattern already established project-wide (RNF09) — no new error-presentation style is introduced specifically for chat.
158	- Every chat session is created with a client-derived title (see FR-010), so the generic placeholder in the side-menu list is a defensive fallback for an unexpected empty title rather than the normal case; the exact wording of both the derived-title preview length and the fallback placeholder is a presentation detail left to implementation.
159	- The composer's existing disabled-by-default rendering (already scaffolded by F000) becomes conditionally enabled by this unit whenever there is non-empty text to send and no response currently in flight or awaiting retry for that conversation — it does not require a separate redesign of the composer itself.

### User Story 5 - Reading history while offline (Priority: P3)

A user without a connection can still read everything they already loaded, but cannot send anything new, and is told clearly why.

**Why this priority**: Explicitly one of the four required prototype states for this screen, and it protects against the worse failure mode of a chat screen that looks broken or loses content when connectivity drops — but it is a secondary concern relative to the core conversation and failure-recovery loops above.

**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by loading a conversation, simulating a loss of connectivity, confirming the existing history stays visible and scrollable, confirming the send control is disabled with an explanatory banner, and confirming sending is not possible until connectivity returns.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** a conversation is already loaded, **When** the device goes offline, **Then** the existing message history remains visible and scrollable, and a banner explains that new messages are blocked.
2. **Given** the device is offline, **When** the user looks at the composer, **Then** the send control is visibly disabled — no message can be sent until the connection returns.
3. **Given** the connection returns, **When** the user resumes using the screen, **Then** the send control re-enables and new messages can be sent normally.
4. **Given** the user has previously opened more than one conversation while online, **When** the device goes offline and the user switches between those previously-opened conversations from the side menu, **Then** each one's cached history is shown exactly as it was left, not just the conversation open at the moment connectivity dropped.

---

### Edge Cases

- The user tries to send an empty or whitespace-only message: the send control stays disabled/inactive, and no request is made.
- A message at or near the backend's maximum length is sent: the system either prevents exceeding that maximum before sending or surfaces the backend's resulting validation error clearly, without losing the text the user typed.
- A message is sent while a previous response in the same conversation is still streaming, or is sitting in the failed/"tap to retry" state: the composer stays disabled until that turn resolves (completes or is retried to a new resolution), so a session never has two responses racing at once.
- The session expires (RF03/RF07's existing "Sessão expirada" behavior) while a response is mid-stream or while viewing history: the existing overlay is shown, history and scroll position are preserved underneath it, and once the user re-authenticates, the conversation resumes exactly where it was — this unit reuses that behavior rather than redefining it.
- The user navigates away from a conversation (e.g., via the side menu) while a response is still streaming: when the user returns to that conversation, the message reflects whatever the backend ultimately recorded for it (complete or failed) rather than being stuck in a stale in-progress state tied to a connection that no longer exists.
- An account has zero conversations yet (first-ever use of chat): the chat screen still shows a ready-to-use empty conversation, and a session is created at the point the first message is actually sent.
- The user retries a failed message that is not the most recent message in the conversation: the retry still succeeds and only affects that specific message's response, leaving every later message in the conversation untouched.
- An account has more conversations than fit in one backend page of `GET /chat/sessions` (more than its default/max `limit`): scrolling to the bottom of the side menu's "CONVERSAS" section fetches the next page via `cursor` rather than silently stopping at the first page.
- The user is offline and selects, from the side menu, a conversation that was never opened while online: no cached data exists for it, so the screen shows the standard no-connection state instead of any content, distinct from the normal offline case of browsing an already-cached conversation.
- Opening the side menu's conversation list, the export job, dashboard, filters, action-plan board, and every other screen or action not named in this feature's scope: unaffected by this unit and not touched by it.

## Requirements *(mandatory)*

### Functional Requirements

- **FR-001**: The system MUST let an authenticated user send a text message in an active conversation (`POST /chat/sessions/:id/messages`) and receive a response generated with the help of the user's own previously captured entries — the response MUST be able to reflect information from a prior entry that the user's message does not itself restate.
- **FR-002**: Every message the user sends and every response the agent produces MUST be persisted as part of the conversation (`chat_messages`) and MUST still be present, in the same order, the next time that conversation is opened — including after the app is closed and reopened (`GET /chat/sessions/:id/messages`).
- **FR-003**: Sending a chat message MUST NOT create a journal entry under any circumstance handled by this unit; the only path from a chat message to a persisted entry is the explicit save action of a later unit (RF10), which this unit does not implement.
- **FR-004**: While a response is being generated, the system MUST render it in a visibly distinct "processing/streaming" state (content revealed progressively, in-progress indicator) and MUST transition it to one of exactly two end states: "complete response" (final text, timestamp shown, no in-progress indicator) or an error state ("Falha ao gerar resposta," shown in place of the timestamp). A response MUST always end in one of these three states — streaming, complete, or error — never left ambiguous.
- **FR-005**: If the response stream is interrupted before completion (connection drop, backend error, or any other cause), the system MUST keep whatever partial text had already arrived visible, together with the failure indication — it MUST NOT remove, hide, or blank out a partial message.
- **FR-006**: A message in the error state MUST be tappable to trigger a retry (`POST /chat/sessions/:id/messages/:userMessageId/retry`) that regenerates the response to that same original question. A retry MUST NOT duplicate the user's original question in the conversation, and MUST go through the same processing/streaming → complete/error states as any other response. Retrying MUST remain available after a retry itself fails, with no fixed limit on the number of attempts, and MUST remain available on any message in the error state regardless of how much later conversation exists after it.
- **FR-007**: While a response in the current conversation is streaming or sitting in the error state awaiting retry, the system MUST keep the message-send control disabled, re-enabling it only once that response reaches a final state (complete, or retried to a new resolution) — so a single conversation never has two responses in flight at once.
- **FR-008**: The side menu MUST show a "CONVERSAS" section listing the user's existing conversations (`GET /chat/sessions`), each with its title and a timestamp, ordered by most recent activity (latest `lastUserMessageAt` first). If the account has more sessions than fit in one backend page, the list MUST fetch further pages via the endpoint's `cursor` as the user scrolls to the bottom of the section, so every conversation stays reachable.
- **FR-009**: The side menu MUST offer a "Novo Chat" action that opens the chat screen in an empty conversation state, ready to accept a first message, without discarding or altering any existing conversation. Selecting an existing conversation from the list MUST open it with its full message history intact, exactly as it was left.
- **FR-010**: A new conversation (`POST /chat/sessions`) MUST only be created at the point a first message is actually sent into an empty conversation state — opening an empty conversation state (via "Novo Chat," or on an account with no conversations yet) MUST NOT by itself create a session with no messages in it. That creation call MUST include a `title` derived from the first message's own text (a short, trimmed preview), so the new conversation has a distinguishable, human-recognizable name in the side menu from the moment it exists — the backend has no auto-titling of its own and no later rename endpoint.
- **FR-011**: While the device is offline, the system MUST keep every previously-opened conversation's history, and the side menu's own "CONVERSAS" list, visible, scrollable, and switchable from the local cache — not only the one conversation that happened to be open when connectivity dropped — MUST disable the send control, and MUST show an explanatory message that new messages are blocked until the connection returns. Selecting a conversation that was never opened while online, while currently offline, MUST show the standard no-connection state rather than any content, since nothing was ever cached for it. Sending MUST become possible again as soon as connectivity is restored, with no manual reset required.
- **FR-012**: The system MUST NOT attempt to create a new conversation or send/retry a message while offline — both actions require a connection and MUST be blocked client-side rather than attempted and failed.
- **FR-013**: The screen MUST reuse the existing session-expiration handling (RF03/RF07's "Sessão expirada" overlay: history and scroll position preserved, re-authentication returning to the same conversation state) rather than introducing a separate expiration treatment for chat.
- **FR-014**: This unit MUST NOT implement the "save message as entry" button (RF10), the proactive-insight card (RF08), AI-persona selection as an active setting (extension, requirements section 2 — persona is only read at session creation as whatever the backend already returns), or any change to the backend, its API contract, or its configuration.

### Key Entities

- **Chat Session**: One conversation thread, identified by an id, with a title derived client-side from its first message at creation time and shown in the side menu's "CONVERSAS" section (a defensive generic placeholder is shown only if a session is ever encountered with an empty title), the persona that was in effect when it was created (read-only here — not user-editable in this unit), and timestamps including when it was created and when it last received a user message (the latter drives the side menu's ordering).
- **Chat Message**: One turn inside a Chat Session — either the user's question or the agent's response — with its content, its position in the conversation, and its status (still arriving, complete, or failed). A failed message is the one eligible for retry; retrying produces a new resolution for the same original question rather than a new message pair.
- **Context used for a response**: The set of the user's own prior entries the agent draws on to ground a given response. It is retrieved automatically for every response and is not displayed to the user as a separate citation list — the prototype defines no such element — but it is what makes a response "grounded" rather than generic, per User Story 1.

## Success Criteria *(mandatory)*

### Measurable Outcomes

- **SC-001**: When a seeded prior entry exists on a topic, a chat message about that topic that does not restate the entry's content still produces a response reflecting that entry's information, in 100% of tested cases.
- **SC-002**: Every sent or retried message ends in exactly one of the three defined states (streaming → complete, or streaming → error) with zero cases observed stuck in an undefined or ambiguous state.
- **SC-003**: In 100% of forced stream-interruption scenarios, the partial response text remains visible on screen together with its failure indication — never disappearing.
- **SC-004**: Across repeated retries of the same failed message, the user's original question appears exactly once in the conversation history, with zero observed duplicates.
- **SC-005**: Conversation history is preserved exactly (same messages, same order) across an app restart and across switching away from and back to a conversation via the side menu, in 100% of tested cases.
- **SC-006**: While offline, 100% of the history of every previously-opened conversation stays readable and switchable from the side menu (not only the one open at disconnect), and the send control is visibly disabled for the entire duration of the outage, re-enabling within one interaction of connectivity returning.
- **SC-007**: On an account with more conversations than one backend page of `GET /chat/sessions` returns, 100% of them remain reachable from the side menu by scrolling, with zero conversations permanently hidden.

## Assumptions

- A conversation ("session") is created lazily, only when the user actually sends a first message into an empty conversation state, rather than eagerly when "Novo Chat" is tapped or when the chat screen is simply opened — this keeps the backend free of empty sessions and matches `POST /chat/sessions` accepting no required `title`. Re-opening the app resumes whichever conversation the user was last in (if any exist); when none exist yet, the screen shows the same empty, ready-to-send state "Novo Chat" also produces.
- The "context" step of the backend's streaming sequence (`message_created -> context -> token* -> done|error`) is an internal signal the client may use to drive its own progress indicator, not a citation list rendered to the user — the prototype defines no UI for displaying which entries were used.
- A session's `personaSnapshot` (requirements section 2's persona extension) is read and stored as whatever the backend returns at session creation; this unit does not add any UI for choosing or changing it.
- Network-error handling for this screen's write calls (send, retry, create session) follows the same retryable/non-retryable pattern already established project-wide (RNF09) — no new error-presentation style is introduced specifically for chat.
- Every chat session is created with a client-derived title (see FR-010), so the generic placeholder in the side-menu list is a defensive fallback for an unexpected empty title rather than the normal case; the exact wording of both the derived-title preview length and the fallback placeholder is a presentation detail left to implementation.
- The composer's existing disabled-by-default rendering (already scaffolded by F000) becomes conditionally enabled by this unit whenever there is non-empty text to send and no response currently in flight or awaiting retry for that conversation — it does not require a separate redesign of the composer itself.

# Feature Specification: P-RF10 — Save a chat message as an entry

**Feature Branch**: `008-chat-message-bookmark` (spec directory only — no git branch was created automatically; none of this repo's extension hooks are configured)

**Created**: 2026-10-21

**Status**: Draft

**Input**: User description: "P-RF10 — Save a chat message as an entry: Let the user turn one of their own chat messages into a journal entry, per docs/input/requirements.md section 1 (RF10) and its acceptance criteria. Prototype state: 'Tela 1 — Bookmark' with its sub-states (prototype extract, section 2.2). Backend: POST /entries with source `chat` and `chatMessageId` (requirements, section 6.2/6.3). Depends on RF01, RF04. Do not implement features of later units, extension features (requirements section 2), or change the backend."

## User Scenarios & Testing *(mandatory)*

### User Story 1 - Turning a message you just wrote into a journal entry (Priority: P1)

While chatting with the agent, the user says something worth keeping on its own — not through the dedicated capture flow (RF01), but right there in the conversation. They tap a bookmark control on their own message, and it becomes a normal, persisted journal entry without leaving the chat or retyping anything.

**Why this priority**: This is the entire premise of RF10 — a second, lightweight path into the journal for moments that happen inside a conversation. Without it, the feature does not exist.

**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by sending a chat message, tapping its bookmark control, and confirming a new entry exists with that message's content, `source` = `chat`, and a `chatMessageId` pointing back to the originating message.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** the user has sent a message in an active conversation, **When** they tap its bookmark control in its resting (`idle`) state, **Then** the control shows a saving indicator (spinner) and, on success, settles into a saved indicator (ochre check) — and a journal entry now exists with that message's text as content, `source` = `chat`, and `chatMessageId` set to that message's id.
2. **Given** a message's bookmark is in the saved state, **When** the user reopens the conversation later (including after restarting the app), **Then** the bookmark still shows the saved state for that message rather than resetting to idle.
3. **Given** the user saves a message, **When** that entry is later viewed anywhere entries are shown, **Then** it is structurally indistinguishable from an entry captured through RF01 — same content, same processing pipeline — except for carrying `source` = `chat` and a non-null `chatMessageId`.

---

### User Story 2 - Saving the same message twice never creates a duplicate (Priority: P1)

A user taps a bookmark that is already saved, or a save silently succeeded on the backend but the app never learned about it (lost connection, a restart mid-save, a reinstalled app with no local record of what was already saved). Either way, retrying never results in two entries for the same message.

**Why this priority**: Called out explicitly as its own acceptance criterion ("saving the same message twice does not create duplicate entries") — without it, a flaky connection or an impatient double-tap would pollute the journal with duplicate content, undermining trust in every other feature that reads entries.

**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by saving a message, then issuing the save again for that same message (e.g., by forcing the app to forget its local saved-state record and tapping the bookmark again), and confirming exactly one entry exists afterward.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** a message has already been saved as an entry, **When** a save for that same message is attempted again through the shared entry-creation flow (not via the `saved` checkmark itself, which is a non-interactive status indicator with no tap handler — see FR-003), **Then** no second entry is created — the existing entry is reused, and the bookmark still ends in the saved state.
2. **Given** the app has no local record of a message's save having already succeeded (e.g., the local record was lost or never updated after a dropped response), **When** the user taps its bookmark and it was in fact already saved on the backend, **Then** the outcome is identical to Scenario 1 — one entry, saved state — never a duplicate.

---

### User Story 3 - A failed save never disrupts the conversation (Priority: P2)

A save attempt fails — most commonly because the device has no connection. The user keeps chatting normally, and the failed bookmark offers a clear way to try again whenever they're ready.

**Why this priority**: RF10's acceptance criteria require this explicitly and anchor it to the same failure-isolation pattern used elsewhere in the product (RF08) — a save failure must be a contained, recoverable glitch, never something that degrades the surrounding chat experience.

**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by forcing a save to fail (e.g., no connection), confirming the bookmark shows an error indicator while the rest of the conversation (sending, receiving, scrolling, other bookmarks) keeps working normally, then tapping the failed bookmark again once the failure condition is removed and confirming the save completes.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** the device has no connection, **When** the user taps a message's bookmark, **Then** the control shows an error indicator (red warning) instead of getting stuck in the saving state, and every other part of the chat screen continues to function exactly as before the attempt.
2. **Given** a bookmark is in the error state, **When** the user taps it again, **Then** it re-attempts the save (returning to the saving indicator) and can reach the saved state once the underlying failure condition is gone.
3. **Given** a bookmark is saving or has failed, **When** the user sends new messages, scrolls, or interacts with other bookmarks in the same conversation, **Then** none of those actions are blocked or delayed by the in-progress or failed save.

---

### User Story 4 - Only your own messages can become entries (Priority: P2)

The bookmark control appears only on the user's own messages — never on the agent's responses.

**Why this priority**: Called out explicitly as an acceptance criterion; getting this wrong would let AI-generated text be filed into the journal as if the user had written it, which is a content-integrity problem, not just a cosmetic one.

**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by inspecting a conversation containing both user and assistant messages and confirming the bookmark control renders only on the user ones.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** a conversation contains both user messages and assistant responses, **When** the chat screen renders them, **Then** a bookmark control is present on every user message and absent from every assistant message, with no exceptions (including insight cards and partial/failed assistant responses).

---

### Edge Cases

- The user taps a bookmark twice in quick succession before the first tap's request resolves: the control ignores the second tap (or treats it as a no-op) rather than firing two concurrent save requests for the same message.
- A save is in flight when the user navigates away from the conversation (e.g., via the side menu) and later returns: the bookmark reflects whatever the save ultimately resolved to (saved or error), not a stale saving indicator tied to a request that already finished.
- The session expires (RF03/RF07's existing "Sessão expirada" behavior) while a save is in flight: the existing overlay takes over as it already does for the rest of the screen; once re-authenticated, the bookmark reflects the save's actual outcome rather than being stuck mid-attempt.
- The underlying message content is at or near the entry content length limit: the save either succeeds normally (chat messages are already capped well below the entry limit) or surfaces the resulting backend validation error on the bookmark as a normal error state — it does not crash or silently drop the attempt.
- A save fails for a reason other than connectivity (e.g., the PII check or embedding step fails after the write): the bookmark still shows the error state and remains retryable, the same as a connectivity failure — the user is not expected to distinguish the underlying cause.
- The user attempts to save an assistant message some other way than the (absent) bookmark control: there is no such path in this unit — assistant messages simply have no save action available anywhere.
- Opening My Records, search, export, the dashboard, the insertion modal, or any other screen or action not named in this feature: unaffected by this unit and not touched by it.

## Requirements *(mandatory)*

### Functional Requirements

- **FR-001**: A bookmark control MUST appear on every user message in the chat and MUST NOT appear on any assistant message, with no exceptions (including insight cards and assistant messages in any status — streaming, complete, or failed).
- **FR-002**: The bookmark control MUST have exactly four visible states — `idle` (resting), `saving` (spinner, in progress), `saved` (ochre check, succeeded), `error` (red warning, failed) — and MUST always be in exactly one of them.
- **FR-003**: Tapping a bookmark in the `idle` or `error` state MUST create a journal entry from that message (`POST /entries`) with `content` equal to the message's own text, `source` = `chat`, and `chatMessageId` set to that message's id, transitioning the control to `saving` and then, on success, to `saved`. The `saved` state is a terminal, non-interactive status indicator — it carries no tap handler, so a message that has reached `saved` cannot be re-tapped to trigger another save.
- **FR-004**: Saving a message whose entry already exists — whether because the control is already in the `saved` state or because the app has no local record that a prior save already succeeded — MUST NOT create a second entry; the existing entry is reused and the control ends in the `saved` state in either case.
- **FR-005**: If a save attempt fails for any reason (no connection, timeout, or any other write failure reported by the backend), the control MUST move to the `error` state rather than remaining in `saving` indefinitely or reverting silently to `idle`, and MUST remain tappable to retry.
- **FR-006**: An in-progress or failed save for one message MUST NOT block, delay, or otherwise affect any other part of the chat screen — sending new messages, receiving responses, scrolling, viewing insights, and the bookmarks on other messages all continue to function normally.
- **FR-007**: While a bookmark is in the `saving` state, further taps on that same bookmark MUST be ignored until that save resolves (to `saved` or `error`) — a message never has two save requests in flight at once.
- **FR-008**: The `saved` state of a message's bookmark MUST be reflected again whenever that conversation is reopened — including after navigating away and back, or restarting the app — for as long as the client can determine the message was already saved.
- **FR-009**: Entry creation triggered from the chat feature MUST go through the same shared entry-creation interface/use case already used elsewhere in the product, and MUST NOT directly import a repository or data source belonging to the entries feature from within the chat feature.
- **FR-010**: This unit MUST NOT implement the proactive-insight mechanism (RF08), the export flow (RF05), the dashboard (RF09), any extension feature (requirements section 2), or any change to the backend, its API contract, or its configuration.

### Key Entities

- **Journal Entry (chat-sourced)**: The same Journal Entry already defined for RF01 — a persisted, immutable record with text content and a creation time — now also reachable with `source` = `chat` and a non-null `chatMessageId` pointing back to the chat message it was saved from. Structurally identical to any other entry; nothing about later screens that read entries needs to treat it differently.
- **Bookmark**: Per-message, per-viewer UI state attached to a user chat message, cycling through `idle` → `saving` → `saved` (success) or `idle`/`error` → `saving` → `error` (failure, retryable). It exists only in relation to a specific message and never itself becomes a persisted record — the entry it may produce is the persisted side effect, not the bookmark itself.

## Success Criteria *(mandatory)*

### Measurable Outcomes

- **SC-001**: Tapping the bookmark on a user message produces a retrievable journal entry with the correct content, `source`, and `chatMessageId` in 100% of success-path attempts.
- **SC-002**: Across repeated or retried save attempts on the same message — including after losing any local record of a prior successful save — exactly one journal entry exists per message in 100% of tested cases, with zero observed duplicates.
- **SC-003**: In 100% of forced save-failure cases (e.g., no connection), the rest of the chat screen remains fully usable throughout the failure, and the failed bookmark reaches the `saved` state once retried after the failure condition is removed.
- **SC-004**: Across all tested conversations, zero bookmark controls appear on assistant messages.
- **SC-005**: A message's `saved` bookmark state is still shown correctly after reopening its conversation (including after an app restart) in 100% of tested cases where the client has a way to know the save already succeeded.

## Assumptions

- The entry's `content` is the chat message's own text, saved verbatim with no edit step offered before saving — the feature is "save this message," not "compose a new entry from this message."
- The entry's `occurredAt` is the chat message's own `createdAt` timestamp (when it was sent), not the moment the user taps the bookmark, so the entry lands at the correct point in the user's timeline.
- Whether a message's bookmark shows `saved` after reopening a conversation (FR-008) relies on a device-local record of which messages this client has already saved; that record is a convenience, not a correctness mechanism — if it is ever missing or wrong (reinstall, cleared cache, a save that succeeded on the backend without the client learning about it), tapping the bookmark again is always safe and resolves to the correct `saved` state without creating a duplicate (FR-004), because the backend itself guarantees the idempotency.
- PII handling and embedding generation for chat-sourced entries follow the exact same pipeline already used for any other entry (RNF02) — this unit introduces no separate consent step or content review specific to chat-origin content.
- No distinct visual treatment (e.g., a badge or label) is added elsewhere in the product to call out chat-sourced entries beyond the `source` field already embedded in the entry's own data — no such element exists in the prototype outside the bookmark control itself.
- "The same shared interface/use case already used elsewhere in the product" (FR-009) refers to whatever cross-feature entry-creation contract RF01 already established (or, if none yet exists in a reusable form, the one this unit must introduce) — the specific shape of that contract is an implementation decision for the planning phase, not a product requirement.
- The `saved` state's checkmark is a terminal, non-interactive status indicator rather than a re-tappable button (FR-003): neither `docs/input/requirements.md` nor the prototype extract says whether a visibly `saved` bookmark can be tapped again, so this was resolved as a reasonable technical decision rather than left open — it keeps the bookmark's state machine simple (no `saved` → `saving`/`error` regression) and avoids a pointless network call once the check mark is showing. FR-004's duplicate-prevention guarantee still protects the real-world path that produces a "second save attempt": a message that renders `idle` only because the local saved-record was lost or never written, not a literal re-tap on a visible `saved` icon.
